column1: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease two 9-inch round pans, line with parchment and grease the parchment.
Whisk the cake flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a medium bowl.
Beat the butter and sugar on medium-high about 3 minutes until fluffy. Add the oil and beat 1 minute, then mix in the yolks and vanilla.
On low speed, add the dry ingredients in three parts, alternating with the buttermilk in two parts, mixing just until combined; the batter will be thick.
In a clean bowl, whip the egg whites and cream of tartar on high to medium-stiff peaks, about 3 minutes.
Gently fold the whites into the batter and divide between the pans.
Bake 27–31 minutes until a toothpick in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pans for 1 hour, then turn out and cool completely on a rack.

For the frosting, beat the butter on medium 2 minutes. Add the sugar, cocoa, 4 tbsp cream, salt and vanilla; beat on low 30 seconds then on high 1 minute, adjusting with more sugar or cream as needed.
Level the cake tops. Spread about 1 cup frosting on the first layer, add the second layer and apply a thin crumb coat over the whole cake.
Chill about 20 minutes to set the crumb coat, then cover with the remaining frosting and decorate with sprinkles if desired.
